data.long_meaning: Jinesh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Jina', which means 'Victor' or 'Conqueror'. In Hindu mythology, Jinesh is the name of Lord Vishnu, who is known as the preserver of the universe. The name is also associated with the Jain Tirthankaras, who are spiritual leaders and teachers in Jainism. The name Jinesh carries the meaning “Lord of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jinesh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: Jinesh is deeply associated with spiritual growth and thriving in the Hindu and Jain traditions. It is a name that resonates with one's connection to Lord Vishnu, the preserver and protector, and to the Jain Tirthankaras, spiritual guides who help one traverse the path of spiritual development. This name stands as a reminder that inner victory and conquest of the soul are the true sources of lasting happiness.

historical_references.reference: Jinesh is a variant of the name Jina, which is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jina' meaning 'victor' or 'conqueror'. This name was commonly used for Jain monks and 24 Tirthankaras (enlightened teachers) in Jainism.
historical_references.context: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion founded by Mahavira around the 6th century BCE. Jinesh is a name with significant religious and historical significance in Jainism.

historical_references.reference: The name Jinesh has also been used in Hindu mythology as a name for a demon king in the Mahabharata epic. In the story, Jinesh, the king of the serpent demons, challenges the hero Bhagadatta to a battle.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic poem that is considered one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, along with the Ramayana. The story of Jinesh and Bhagadatta is a part of the Bhagavad Gita, which forms a part of the Mahabharata.
